verdict.rationale: a-Shell ships its own Apple Shortcuts actions, such as `Execute Command`, `Put File` and `Get File`, and they can be forced to run "in Extension" rather than in the app. That lets scripted command sequences run without the user driving the terminal. However, these are one-off actions invoked from Shortcuts. a-Shell documents no recurring schedule, trigger system or background daemon of its own, and the docs warn that extension mode "won't always work." Missing for 10: a native scheduler or recurring triggers, documented background execution guarantees, any agent-style autonomous automation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: You can write complex Shortcuts to download, process and release files using a-Shell commands.
`Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order.
You can force a specific shortcut to run "in App" or "in Extension", with the warning that it won't always work.
